title: Finite-stage detection of a zero limit cohomology class
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preordered set and let $D:I^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sch}$ be an inverse diagram of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms. Let $(X,(f_i))$ be a limit cone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For each $i$, let $F_i$ be an abelian sheaf on $(D_i)_{\acute{e}t}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], with maps $\varphi_f:D(f^{\mathrm{op}})^{-1}F_i\to F_j$ for $f:i\to j$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] satisfying the canonical inverse-image identity and composition laws. Let $G:I\to\operatorname{Ab}(X_{\acute{e}t})$ be identified objectwise with $f_i^{-1}F_i$ by isomorphisms, its arrows being inverse-image composition followed by pullback of $\varphi_f$. Let $L$ be a colimit cocone on $G$, with coprojections $\iota_i$. Fix $p\ge0$. Let $H:I\to\operatorname{Ab}$ have specified object isomorphisms $e_i:H_i\cong H^p(D_i,F_i)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and arrows conjugate to $H^p(\varphi_f)\circ D(f^{\mathrm{op}})^*$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Let $B$ be a cocone on $H$ with an isomorphism $e:B_{\mathrm{pt}}\cong H^p(X,L_{\mathrm{pt}})$ such that, for every $i$, its leg $b_i$ satisfies $e\circ b_i=H^p(\iota_i)\circ f_i^*\circ e_i$, including the specified identification $G_i\cong f_i^{-1}F_i$. Then $\forall i\in I\;\forall x\in H_i:\ b_i(x)=0\Rightarrow\exists j\in I\;\exists(f:i\to j):\ H(f)(x)=0$. This asserts detection of zero only.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09YQ (theorem-colimit), via Lemma Tag 0EYL (lemma-colimit-affine-sites) and sites-cohomology.tex Lemma Tag 09YP (lemma-colimit); the qcqs finite-affine-cover reduction in parent steps 5-8 uses Tag 0A50 (lemma-mayer-vietoris). Source pages checked online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09YQ, /09YP, /0EYL and /0A50 on 2026-10-12.

proof.text: *The system on $X$ and the map.* For $i'\ge i$ we have $f_i=f_{i'i}\circ f_{i'}$; let $\psi_{i'i}:f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i\cong f_{i'}^{-1}f_{i'i}^{-1}\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{f_{i'}^{-1}\varphi_{i'i}}f_{i'}^{-1}\mathcal F_{i'}$, the first arrow the inverse of the isomorphism $c_{f_{i'i},f_{i'}}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. The cocycle condition $\varphi_{i''i}=\varphi_{i''i'}\circ f_{i''i'}^{-1}\varphi_{i'i}$, the naturality of $c$ and its compatibility with triple composites ([lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], uniqueness of $c$ compatible with the units) give $\psi_{i''i}=\psi_{i''i'}\circ\psi_{i'i}$, so $(f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i,\psi)$ is a directed system in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ and $\mathcal F=\varinjlim f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i$ exists [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with coprojections $\iota_i$. Put $\theta_i=H^p(\iota_i)\circ f_i^*:H^p((X_i)_{\Et},\mathcal F_i)\to H^p(X_{\Et},f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i)\to H^p(X_{\Et},\mathcal F)$ ([def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]). The transition maps of the system $(H^p((X_i)_{\Et},\mathcal F_i))_i$ are $H^p(\varphi_{i'i})\circ f_{i'i}^*$; by the naturality and composition parts of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], $f_{i'}^*\circ H^p(\varphi_{i'i})\circ f_{i'i}^*=H^p(f_{i'}^{-1}\varphi_{i'i})\circ f_{i'}^*\circ f_{i'i}^*=H^p(\psi_{i'i})\circ f_i^*$, so $\theta_{i'}\circ H^p(\varphi_{i'i})\circ f_{i'i}^*=H^p(\iota_{i'}\circ\psi_{i'i})\circ f_i^*=\theta_i$. Hence the $\theta_i$ induce the canonical map $\theta:\varinjlim_iH^p((X_i)_{\Et},\mathcal F_i)\to H^p(X_{\Et},\mathcal F)$ of the statement; the claim is that $\theta$ is bijective.

source.place: Paragraph after Definition definition-inverse-system-sheaves (line 7316: 'This turns $f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i$ into a system of sheaves on $X_\etale$ over $I$ (it is a good exercise to check this)') and Theorem Tag 09YQ (theorem-colimit, line 7400)

proof.text: *Passing to a cofinal part of $I$.* For $i_0\in I$ the subset $I_{\ge i_0}$ is directed and cofinal in $I$. The limit of $(X_i)_{i\ge i_0}$ is again $X$ with the same projections (a cone over $I_{\ge i_0}$ extends uniquely to $I$: for each $i$ choose $j\ge i,i_0$ and compose its leg at $j$ with $X_j\to X_i$; directedness and the cone equations make this independent of $j$; [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] gives the limit), the colimit $\mathcal F$ is unchanged, and so is $\varinjlim H^p((X_i)_{\Et},\mathcal F_i)$ together with $\theta$, by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory](1) applied to the inclusion $I_{\ge i_0}\subseteq I$ (every $i$ has some $i'\ge i,i_0$). So in proving the theorem we may replace $I$ by $I_{\ge i_0}$ for any $i_0$.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09YQ; standard reduction, written out by the agent

proof.text: *Affine case, translation to the affine etale sites.* Assume every $X_i$ is affine; then $X$ is affine ([lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], last clause). For each scheme $T\in\{X,X_i\}$ let $T_{affine,\Et}$ be the small affine etale site and $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G|_{aff}$ the equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-topos]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-colimit] the base change functors $u_{i'i}$, $u_i$ make $((X_i)_{affine,\Et})_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}$ a system of sites as in [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites] whose colimit site is $X_{affine,\Et}$ with the functors $u_i$; write $g_{i'i}:(X_{i'})_{affine,\Et}\to(X_i)_{affine,\Et}$ and $g_i:X_{affine,\Et}\to(X_i)_{affine,\Et}$ for the morphisms of sites they define [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Claim: for $h\in\{f_{i'i},f_i\}$ with corresponding $g$ and $u$, $(h^{-1}\mathcal G)|_{aff}\cong g^{-1}(\mathcal G|_{aff})$ naturally in $\mathcal G$, compatibly with composition. Proof: for an abelian sheaf $\mathcal H$ on the source etale site and an affine $V$ etale over the target, $(h_*\mathcal H)(V)=\mathcal H(V\times h)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and $V\times h=u(V)$ is affine, so $(h_*\mathcal H)|_{aff}=g_*(\mathcal H|_{aff})$ (both are $V\mapsto\mathcal H(u(V))$), naturally in $\mathcal H$. Thus under the equivalences $|_{aff}$ the functors $h_*$ and $g_*=u^s$ correspond; their left adjoints $h^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $g^{-1}=u_s$ then correspond up to a unique isomorphism compatible with the units (a left adjoint is unique up to unique isomorphism, and an equivalence transports adjunctions), and uniqueness gives compatibility with composites ($u_{i'}\circ u_{i'i}=u_i$, $f_i=f_{i'i}\circ f_{i'}$, matched with [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]). Consequently $(\mathcal F_i|_{aff},\varphi_{i'i}|_{aff})$ (transported along these isomorphisms) is a system of abelian sheaves on the sites $(X_i)_{affine,\Et}$ satisfying the cocycle condition of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-colimit-of-sites], and since an equivalence preserves colimits, $\mathcal F|_{aff}\cong\varinjlim g_i^{-1}(\mathcal F_i|_{aff})$ compatibly with the coprojections.

source.place: Proof of Theorem Tag 09YQ (line 7413: 'By Topologies, Lemma 04HR we can compute the cohomology of $\mathcal F$ on $X_{affine,\etale}$'), with Lemma Tag 0EYL; the identification of the inverse images across the equivalence is left implicit in the source and written out here by the agent

proof.text: *Affine case, conclusion.* Keep the assumption of the previous step and fix $i\in I$. $X_i$ (with the identity) is an object of $(X_i)_{affine,\Et}$, and $u_{i'i}(X_i)=X_{i'}$, $u_i(X_i)=X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-colimit-of-sites] applied to the system of the previous step and the object $X_i$, $\varinjlim_{i'\ge i}H^p(X_{i'},\mathcal F_{i'}|_{aff})\to H^p(X,\mathcal F|_{aff})$ (cohomology over objects of the affine sites) is an isomorphism, the maps being pullback along $g_{i'}$ followed by the coprojection. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-topos] (cohomology clause, with $U=X_{i'}$ final in $(X_{i'})_{\Et}$, resp. $U=X$) the source terms are $H^p((X_{i'})_{\Et},\mathcal F_{i'})$ and the target is $H^p(X_{\Et},\mathcal F)$, functorially in the sheaf; since these isomorphisms are functorial and the pullbacks are both induced by the adjunction units on injective resolutions, which correspond under the equivalences by the previous step, the map becomes $\theta$ restricted to $I_{\ge i}$ ([def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]). By step 2 ($I_{\ge i}$ cofinal), $\theta$ is an isomorphism. This proves the theorem when all $X_i$ are affine, and by step 2 also when $X_{i_0}$ is affine for some $i_0$ (then every $X_i$, $i\ge i_0$, is affine, being affine over the affine $X_{i_0}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]).

source.place: Proof of Theorem Tag 09YQ: 'the result by a combination of Lemma 0EYL and Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 09YP'

proof.text: *Restriction to an open of a stage.* Let $i_0\in I$ and $W_{i_0}\subseteq X_{i_0}$ a quasi-compact open; for $i\ge i_0$ let $W_i=f_{ii_0}^{-1}(W_{i_0})$ and $W=f_{i_0}^{-1}(W_{i_0})$. Then $W_i$ is quasi-compact (preimage of a quasi-compact open under the affine, hence quasi-compact, $f_{ii_0}$) and quasi-separated (open in the quasi-separated $X_i$), the restricted transition maps are affine and $W=\varprojlim_{i\ge i_0}W_i$ ([lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], open clause). With $j_{W_i}$, $j_W$ the open immersions (etale), $\mathcal F_i|_{W_i}=j_{W_i}^{-1}\mathcal F_i$ and the maps $\varphi_{i'i}|$ obtained by applying $j_{W_{i'}}^{-1}$ and the isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] ($f_{i'i}\circ j_{W_{i'}}=j_{W_i}\circ f_{i'i}|$) form a system on $(W_i)$ as in the statement, and $\varinjlim(f_i|_W)^{-1}(\mathcal F_i|_{W_i})\cong j_W^{-1}\varinjlim f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i=\mathcal F|_W$, because $j_W^{-1}$, a left adjoint of $j_{W*}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], preserves colimits [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] and $j_W^{-1}f_i^{-1}\cong(f_i|_W)^{-1}j_{W_i}^{-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], compatibly with the transition maps. So the data restricted to $W_{i_0}$ again satisfy the hypotheses of the theorem, with limit $W$ and colimit sheaf $\mathcal F|_W$; we call this the restricted system.

source.place: Lemma Tag 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit) part (2); the restriction of the system of sheaves is written out by the agent

proof.text: *Induction by Mayer-Vietoris.* Let $i_0\in I$ and $X_{i_0}=U_{i_0}\cup V_{i_0}$ with $U_{i_0},V_{i_0}$ quasi-compact opens, and suppose the theorem holds for the restricted systems (step 5) of $U_{i_0}$, $V_{i_0}$ and $U_{i_0}\cap V_{i_0}$ (quasi-compact, $X_{i_0}$ being quasi-separated). For $i\ge i_0$ the Mayer-Vietoris sequences [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris] of $(X_i,U_i,V_i,\mathcal F_i)$ form a directed system of long exact sequences: the transition maps $H^p(\varphi_{i'i})\circ f_{i'i}^*$ are morphisms of long exact sequences by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris-pullback] (for $f_{i'i}$, with $U_{i'}=f_{i'i}^{-1}U_i$, $V_{i'}=f_{i'i}^{-1}V_i$) and the functoriality in the sheaf of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris] (for $\varphi_{i'i}$). Its colimit is a long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact], and the maps $\theta$ (pullback along $f_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris-pullback], then the coprojection, by functoriality in the sheaf) form a morphism from it to the Mayer-Vietoris sequence of $(X,U,V,\mathcal F)$, $U=f_{i_0}^{-1}U_{i_0}$, $V=f_{i_0}^{-1}V_{i_0}$, the terms over $U$, $V$, $U\cap V$ being identified with those of the restricted systems by step 5. In each segment $\varinjlim H^{p-1}(U_i\cap V_i)\to\varinjlim H^p(X_i)\to\varinjlim H^p(U_i)\oplus\varinjlim H^p(V_i)\to\varinjlim H^p(U_i\cap V_i)$ (with $\varinjlim H^{p-1}(U_i)\oplus\varinjlim H^{p-1}(V_i)$ in front; for $p=0$ the terms of degree $-1$ are $0$) the four outer maps are isomorphisms by hypothesis, so the middle map $\theta$ for $X$ is an isomorphism by the five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50 (lemma-mayer-vietoris); this reduction is not in the source (agent-written: Stacks' proof of 09YQ applies Lemma 09YP to the object $X_i$ of $(X_i)_{affine,\etale}$, which exists only when $X_i$ is affine)

proof.text: *Separated case.* Suppose $X_{i_0}$ is separated for some $i_0$ and covered by $n$ affine opens; we show the theorem by induction on $n$ (for all systems). By step 2 we may index by $I_{\ge i_0}$. If $n=0$, the chosen stage and every stage on its tail are empty (a scheme mapping to the empty scheme is empty); the limit is empty and all abelian sheaf cohomology groups are zero, so the comparison is an isomorphism. If $n=1$, $X_{i_0}$ is affine: step 4. If $n\ge2$, write $X_{i_0}=U_{i_0}\cup V_{i_0}$ with $U_{i_0}$ one of the affines and $V_{i_0}$ the union of the other $n-1$. Then $U_{i_0}\cap V_{i_0}$ is a union of $n-1$ affine opens [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection] and separated, $V_{i_0}$ is separated and a union of $n-1$ affines, and $U_{i_0}$ is affine; the restricted systems (step 5) of these three opens satisfy the theorem by induction and by step 4, so step 6 gives the theorem for $X$.

source.place: agent-written reduction (the standard induction on the number of affines, cf. the proof of Lemma Tag 03Q5 (lemma-colimit) sketched in the source)

proof.text: *General case.* $X_{i_0}$ ($i_0\in I$ arbitrary) is quasi-compact, so it is covered by $n$ affine opens; induct on $n$. For $n=0$ use the empty-scheme argument of step 7. For $n=1$ use step 4. For $n\ge2$ write $X_{i_0}=U_{i_0}\cup V_{i_0}$ with $U_{i_0}$ affine and $V_{i_0}$ a union of $n-1$ affines. $V_{i_0}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so its restricted system satisfies the theorem by induction; $U_{i_0}\cap V_{i_0}$ is a quasi-compact open of the affine (so separated) $U_{i_0}$, hence separated and a finite union of affines, so its restricted system satisfies the theorem by step 7; $U_{i_0}$ is handled by step 4. Step 6 gives the theorem for $X$. This proves the theorem for every $p\ge0$.

Take a stage class x with b_i(x)=0. Steps 1-8 construct the canonical comparison and prove its injectivity without using the parent continuity theorem as a premise. Hence the image of x in the filtered group colimit is zero. Equality in a filtered group colimit is witnessed at a common later stage. Apply this to x and zero from the same stage i to obtain j and f:i->j with H(f)(x)=0. Additivity identifies the transition of zero with zero. No representative of an arbitrary class of B.pt is required.
